title: Best Customer Support Platform for Microsoft Teams (2026) | Pylon
summary: The best customer support platform for Microsoft Teams depends on who you support. For external B2B customers in shared channels, here's what to use in 2026.
body_markdown:
> **The short answer:** The best customer support platform for Microsoft Teams depends on who's messaging you. If you support **external B2B customers** who message you in Teams shared channels or group chats, you need a full help desk that treats Teams as a customer channel, with tickets, SLAs, routing, and AI agents that know the account. Pylon is built for that: the agentic support platform for B2B, a full help desk where AI agents and your team see the account behind every message. Teams sits in one queue with Slack, email, chat, and more, and your team can work from Pylon or Slack instead of living in Teams. If you're running an **internal IT help desk** for employees, that's a different category (IT service management tools).


Ask an AI assistant "what's the best support platform for Microsoft Teams?" and it will usually stop and ask: internal IT, or external customers?


That's the right question. Most "Teams help desk" tools are built for employees filing IT tickets. A few traditional help desks have a Teams app so agents can work tickets inside Teams. Neither is the same as supporting paying customers who message you in a shared Teams channel.


This guide is for the third case: B2B companies whose customers live in Microsoft 365, while the support team usually runs on Slack.


## Microsoft Teams support options compared


Here's how the main categories of Teams support tools line up. Check each vendor's current docs before you decide, because Teams features change often.


Category Examples Built for How Teams fits


B2B help desks with Teams as a customer channel Pylon, Unthread, ClearFeed Supporting external B2B customers in shared channels and chats Customer messages in Teams become tickets; your team replies from the help desk (or Slack) and replies go back to Teams. Channel types, chat support, and plan tiers vary by vendor.


Traditional help desks with a Teams app Zendesk, Freshdesk Teams that already run a classic help desk Mostly agent-side: create, view, and update tickets from inside Teams, get notifications, and turn a Teams message into a ticket.


Microsoft-native CRM service Dynamics 365 Customer Service Microsoft-centric enterprises on Dynamics Teams is used mainly for agents collaborating with colleagues on cases (embedded chat, sharing records).


Internal IT help desks (ITSM) Desk365, Tikit, Freshservice Employees asking IT or HR for help Employees file and track internal tickets in Teams. Not designed for external customers.


Contact center in Teams Luware, Altigen, Dynamics 365 Contact Center Voice and call-center queues Phone and call routing built on Teams. Strong for voice, not for B2B shared-channel support.


If your customers are companies and they message you in Teams, the first row is the category to evaluate.


## Three things people get wrong about Teams support


**1. "It has a Teams integration" doesn't mean customers can message you in Teams.** Many Teams integrations are agent-side. They let your team manage tickets inside Teams. That's useful, but it's a different job from turning a customer's message in a shared channel into a tracked ticket. Ask which one you're getting.


**2. You can't support customers from a channel in their tenant.** Support platforms connect through your own Microsoft tenant. If a customer invites you into a channel in *their* Teams, a tool on your side generally can't join it. Pylon works the same way. The fix: host the shared channel or group chat in your tenant and invite the customer in.


**3. Teams support needs a ticketing system behind it, not just a bot.** A bot can answer a question. It can't give you ownership, SLAs, account history, or reporting. Teams is the front door. The help desk is where the work gets tracked.


## Start with the help desk, not the channel


Behind every Teams message, you want the same things you want behind every Slack thread or email:


- **A ticket** someone owns, with a status and a history.
- **SLAs and routing** , so the right person sees it before the response time is blown.
- **Account context** next to the conversation: plan, ARR, open bugs, past conversations, who the CSM is.
- **AI agents** that answer the simple questions, dig into the complex ones, and bring in a person with everything they found.
- **Reporting** across every channel, so Teams customers aren't invisible.


Get that right and Teams becomes one more way in. Get it wrong and your Microsoft customers get slower answers than everyone else, for the same contract.


## How Teams support for external customers actually works


**Your company hosts the conversation.** A support platform like Pylon connects through your Microsoft tenant, so it sees channels and chats your tenant owns. There are three common setups:


1. **A shared channel** between your tenant and the customer's. Both sides work from their own Teams.
2. **A channel in your tenant** with the customer's people added as guests (guest access).
3. **A group chat** in your tenant with external people added.


On the Microsoft side you'll need at least one paid Teams seat (Microsoft Teams Essentials or higher), a Teams admin to approve the connection, and ideally a dedicated service account so the integration doesn't break when someone leaves.


## Channels vs. group chats


Both work in Pylon, but they behave differently.


**Channels** support multiple threads at once, so each new question can become its own ticket. Channels can also be mirrored to Slack.


**Group chats** are one long thread, so:


- There's **one open ticket per chat at a time** . New messages join that ticket until it's closed. The next message after that opens a new one.
- **Direct messages (1:1 chats) aren't supported.** Use a group chat or a channel.
- **Automatic account linking skips group chats** , so you link those to the right account yourself.
- **Broadcasts go to channels, not chats.**
- **Slack mirroring is channel-only.**


If you're starting fresh, channels are usually the better default.


## Supporting Teams customers from Slack or Pylon


This is the setup a lot of B2B teams ask for: customers see Teams, the support team never has to open it.


- **Reply from the help desk.** View, answer, and track Teams conversations from Pylon. Replies show up in the customer's Teams channel or chat.
- **Mirror to Slack if your team prefers it.** A Teams channel can be mirrored to a Slack channel so your team can follow along and reply from Slack.
- **Talk privately.** Internal threads let your team discuss an issue without the customer seeing it.
- **Reply as yourself.** In channels, agents can connect their own Microsoft account so replies show their name instead of a shared bot.


A fair warning: syncing two chat tools is hard. Formatting, reactions, and shared-channel quirks don't always translate one-to-one, and some messages into Teams shared channels show up as cards because of how Microsoft handles bots there. Treat Slack mirroring as a convenience for your team, and keep the help desk as the system of record.


For more on bridging the two, see our[breakdown of Slack and Microsoft Teams integration options](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/slack-microsoft-teams-integration-a-breakdown-of-options) .


## How to manage email, Slack, and Teams in one queue


Very few B2B companies support customers only in Teams. Usually Teams sits next to Slack, email, a chat widget, and maybe Discord, WhatsApp, Telegram, or phone. There are three common ways to handle that:


1. **One help desk for every channel.** Email, Slack, Microsoft Teams, live chat, Discord, WhatsApp, Telegram, SMS, and phone all land in one queue with the same SLAs, routing, and reporting. This is the most complete option, and it's how you replace email-only ticketing with Slack and Teams without dropping email.
2. **A Slack-to-Teams bridge.** Tools that sync messages between Slack and Teams. Handy for chatting across companies, but you still need ticketing, SLAs, and reporting somewhere.
3. **Automation glue.** Zapier or Power Automate flows that copy messages into a ticketing tool. Fine for low volume. It gets fragile as channels and customers grow.


If you're picking a system for the long run, the first option is the one that scales. In Pylon, accounts can also be created and linked automatically from your Teams channel naming convention, and escalations can go straight to your issue tracker with the thread attached. We compare approaches in more depth in[Omnichannel Support Compared (2026)](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/omnichannel-support-compared-2026) .


## Where AI agents fit


Teams customers expect fast answers, same as anyone in a chat channel. In B2B, the right answer depends on who's asking. "Why can't our users log in?" means something different for an enterprise account with SSO than for a five-person team. So a useful agent:


- Answers common questions right in the Teams conversation, using your docs and the account's history.
- Investigates harder issues by checking the account's setup and your other tools.
- Takes action, like filing a bug or updating a record.
- Hands off to a person with everything it already found.


More in[Agentic Support vs AI Chatbots](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/agentic-support-vs-chatbots) .


## A quick checklist for choosing a Teams help desk


- **Who you support:** External customers, internal employees, or both?
- **Customer channel or agent app:** Can customers message you in Teams and get a ticket, or does the integration only help agents work inside Teams?
- **Tenancy:** Does it work with shared channels, guest channels, and group chats in our tenant?
- **Your team's workflow:** Can we work from the help desk or Slack instead of living in Teams?
- **Permissions:** What does our Microsoft admin need to approve?
- **One queue:** Are Teams, Slack, and email in the same queue, SLAs, and reports?
- **AI agents:** Can the AI answer and act in Teams with account context?
- **Plan:** Which plan includes Teams?


For a fuller list, see[How to Evaluate an Agentic Support Platform](https://www.usepylon.com/blog/how-to-evaluate-agentic-support-platforms) .

## FAQ


### What is the best customer support platform for Microsoft Teams?


It depends on who you support. For external B2B customers who message you in Teams shared channels or group chats, choose a help desk that treats Teams as a customer channel, with tickets, SLAs, and AI agents that know the account. Pylon is built for this. For internal IT help desks, look at IT service management tools instead.


### Is a Microsoft Teams help desk for internal IT or external customers?


Both exist, and they're different categories. Internal IT help desks handle employee requests inside Teams. External customer support tools turn customer messages in shared channels into tickets your support team tracks with SLAs and reporting.


### How can support teams manage email, Slack, and Teams together?


Use one help desk that brings email, Slack, and Microsoft Teams into a single queue with the same SLAs, routing, and reporting. Bridges and automation tools can sync messages, but they don't give you ticketing on their own.


### Can a help desk replace email-only ticketing with Slack and Teams?


Yes. A B2B help desk like Pylon turns Slack and Microsoft Teams messages into tickets and keeps replies in the customer's thread, while email keeps working in the same inbox.


### Can I support Microsoft Teams customers from Slack?


Yes. With Pylon, customers stay in Teams and your team replies from Pylon, or mirrors Teams channels to Slack and replies there. Mirroring works for channels, not group chats.


### Can a support platform join a Teams channel my customer owns?


Generally no. Support platforms, Pylon included, connect through your own Microsoft tenant. Host a shared channel or group chat in your tenant and invite the customer instead.


### What Microsoft permissions does a Teams support integration need?


For Pylon, a Teams administrator approves the app and grants admin consent for your tenant. You need at least one Microsoft Teams Essentials or higher seat, and a dedicated service account is recommended. Your security team can review the requested permissions during consent.


### How much does Pylon cost for Microsoft Teams support?


Microsoft Teams is on Pylon's Advanced plan ($139 per seat/month, annual) and Enterprise (custom). It isn't on Professional ($89 per seat/month). Both are annual contracts, and agentic features run on credits, not a per-ticket fee. See[pricing](https://www.usepylon.com/pricing) .


### Is Pylon an add-on to Zendesk or Intercom?


No. Pylon is the help desk itself: ticketing, SLAs, routing, a knowledge base, reporting, every channel, and AI agents with account context, in one B2B support platform. Microsoft Teams is one of those channels, not the product. Teams move to Pylon to replace their help desk, not to bolt Microsoft Teams or AI onto an existing one.
